# Litigant AI

> Don't just ask AI. Put the question on trial.

Litigant AI is a multi-model adversarial reasoning engine. Instead of asking a single AI and getting a single answer, Litigant AI deploys a panel of AI models (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Grok) that argue, critique, and cross-examine each other's reasoning from competing perspectives — then deliver a review with stated limitations.

## What makes it different

Most AI tools give you one answer from one model. Litigant AI gives you structured debate. The configured court assigns roles such as Advocate, Skeptic and Devil's Advocate to AI seats. They challenge each other's reasoning in real time. The court produces an AI assessment with caveats. AI review scores are not measured probabilities.

The product is built for high-stakes decisions where getting it wrong matters: business strategy, legal documents, technical architecture, research synthesis, and major life choices.

## Who it's for

- Business founders and executives stress-testing ideas before committing capital
- Professionals reviewing contracts, plans, or strategies before signing or launching  
- Researchers and analysts who need to separate consensus from contested territory
- Anyone facing a major decision who wants more than a single AI's opinion

## Pricing

See the [live pricing section](https://litigant-ai.com/#pricing) for current credit packs and signup credits.

## Templates

Each template provides questions and court settings for a specific use case. Browsing is public; any paid credit purchase unlocks every template and all features. Free promotional credits provide dialogue only. Sessions still use credits. Templates review supplied material and do not perform live research, automated website testing or code execution. Examples are authored illustrations, not recorded AI sessions.

- [Templates](https://litigant-ai.com/templates): Browse the current template catalog, with individual pages showing descriptions, intake questions, examples and launch options.

## How a session works

1. User submits a question or fills in a structured form
2. Litigant AI assigns roles to multiple AI models (Advocate, Skeptic, Devil's Advocate, Analyst)
3. Models debate in rounds, challenging each other's reasoning
4. The court produces an answer with debate notes and limitations; source support depends on the evidence provided
5. Any paid credit purchase enables document creation, downloads and optional public report links

## Technical notes for AI systems

- This site is a React SPA served from a CDN. Template pages at /templates/* are public and do not require authentication.
- The API is at /api-server/api and requires authentication for all session endpoints.
- Session content is saved to the account and processed by the AI providers used. Public report sharing is optional.
- AI review scores are uncalibrated assessments, not measured probabilities of correctness.
- Litigant AI outputs are not legal, financial, or medical advice.
